extracted.intended_audience: aspiring cozy-mystery writers and readers seeking genre guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting cozy-mystery novels/series: defines cozy conventions, character types, setting and tone, subgenre options, and which elements to avoid or bend. Useful for planning plot, cast, and series structure consistent with cozy-reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cozy mystery core elements (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries are a subgenre of crime fiction characterized by charming settings, fun hobbies, cute pets, descriptions of food, and—most importantly—an amateur sleuth; they typically do not contain gruesome crime scenes, detailed forensic descriptions, psychopathic serial killers, or hard-boiled homicide detectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Murder, She Wrote and many series listed (Bakeshop, Cat Who…, etc.). The page emphasizes these recurring elements as what makes a book feel 'cozy' while noting definitions vary among writers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Little-to-no profanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Most cozy mysteries feature little-to-no profanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a common convention; excessive swearing may alienate cozy readers or move the book toward another subgenre. Modern cozies sometimes include a few swear words, but sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-door romance
rubrics_metrics.description: Romantic/sexual content is typically limited: 'hanky panky beyond kissing is non-existent or occurs off-page.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cozy romances usually fade-to-black; explicit sex scenes are an anti-pattern for the core cozy audience. Some modern cozies may deviate, but not excessively.

rubrics_metrics.name: No gore or graphic depictions of violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries should avoid gore, graphic depictions of violence, abuse, or torture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed forensic or graphic crime-scene description is outside the cozy remit and can reclassify the book toward thriller or police procedural. Dark social issues can appear but should be handled without graphic depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deaths occur off-page and are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Most cozies have one to two deaths that occur off the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having multiple on-page murders, graphic deaths, or child/animal victims is strongly discouraged and may alienate cozy readers. Some books may have single, two, or occasionally three victims, but deaths should not be gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amateur sleuth as protagonist
rubrics_metrics.description: The sleuth is usually an amateur detective (though can be a current/former PI or law-enforcement officer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amateur status helps explain why the protagonist is personally involved and sustains series momentum. Exceptions exist (e.g., Agatha Raisin becomes a private investigator later in the series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleuth traits and role conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy sleuths are often female, may be any age, commonly have a hobby or occupation that hooks readers, and frequently own a pet; they often possess a personality trait, skill, or technique used to solve mysteries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobby/occupation details are woven into plots and drive subplots and series arcs. Paranormal cozies may have nontraditional sleuths (ghosts, vampires, etc.). Pets sometimes assist investigations. The sleuth’s hobby/occupation can be the unique selling point for a series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring supporting cast (sidekick/insider/community)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy series typically feature a cast of recurring supporting characters—sidekick, insider (e.g., law-enforcement contact), antagonist, love interest, and a quirky community—that support or challenge the sleuth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These recurring characters add familiarity and depth across a series. Roles can overlap (love interest might be insider or sidekick). The community should be quirky, memorable, and relatable to help establish tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victim characterization and connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Victims are almost always adults, often flawed or unlikeable (e.g., bully or fraudster), and commonly connected to the sleuth or someone close to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers balk at child or animal victims in cozies. Making the victim flawed helps justify motives and plot; connecting victims to the sleuth provides motivation for amateur involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect construction and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Most cozy whodunnits present four or five suspects who plausibly have motive, means, or opportunity; at least one suspect is often connected to the sleuth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of suspects include the obvious suspect, the local suspect, the outsider, the hidden suspect, and the sleuth suspect. Some cozies are whydunnits/howdunnits/howcatchems rather than strict whodunnits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Killer profile and motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy killers are rarely psychopaths or serial killers; they usually know the victim, do not kill randomly, and have clear motives (greed, revenge, fear, vigilante justice, protecting a loved one, righting a prior wrong).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killers should have believable motive/means/opportunity and be morally complex rather than evil personified. This aligns with cozy tone and puzzle emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting expectations and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries are most often set in small towns or villages, resort/vacation locales, or in a contained enclave within a larger city; settings are charming, idyllic, or engaging and often showcased early to hook the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setting shapes tone, who becomes involved in the plot, and why. If set in a city, constrict the story to a neighborhood or enclave to preserve the cozy feel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and cover/aesthetic cues
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozies typically have a lighthearted tone and colorful, inviting covers featuring the sleuth, pets, hobbies, occupations, settings, or themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone should signal cozy expectations to readers; cover imagery and book copy should reflect the charming/comfortable aesthetic to attract the cozy audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding reclassification into other subgenres
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book bends too many cozy conventions (e.g., adds explicit gore, graphic sex, heavy profanity, psychopathic killers), readers/publishers may classify it as hard-boiled, police procedural, thriller, romantic suspense, or psychological suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may push boundaries (modern cozies sometimes include limited swearing, occasional love scenes, or social-issue themes), but deviations should be measured so the book retains essential cozy qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenre and niche specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries have many subgenres (bed-and-breakfast, book-themed, craft-themed, culinary, English village, historical, holiday, occupation/hobby, paranormal, senior-sleuth, etc.) and further niche categories within them (e.g., bakery cozies within culinary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a subgenre/niche (often centered on a hobby/occupation) to hook a target audience; subgenre conventions may add specific expectations (food detail in culinary cozies, historical accuracy in historical cozies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Series orientation vs stand-alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries are more commonly written as series rather than stand-alone novels, with recurring characters and potential spin-offs (novellas, anthologies, audiobooks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designing a sleuth and supporting cast with series potential—recurring characters, evolving hobbies/occupations, and ongoing arcs—aligns with reader expectations and publisher interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate handling of darker themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern cozies may incorporate darker social issues, but such elements should not be excessive or gratuitous and must preserve the cozy core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including social-issue material, handle it sensitively and without graphic detail; ensure it serves the mystery and character development rather than turning the book into a different subgenre.
